englishSamples: Hey, can you come over here?
I found diamonds near the lava lake.
Watch out, there's a creeper behind you!
Do you have any spare iron?
Follow me, the village is this way.
Where did you put the chest with the food?
Can you hear me? My microphone might be broken.
Good game everyone, see you later.

components.notes: Brazilian Portuguese. Tested >>pt<<, >>pt_BR<<, >>pt_br<< and >>pt_PT<<: >>pt_BR<< gives consistent Brazilian Portuguese (jogando, trem, ônibus, você) and the most complete output; >>pt<< gives European Portuguese but drops clauses; >>pt_br<< is Brazilian but less consistent; >>pt_PT<< produces a Spanish/Catalan/Italian mix.

components.notes: Transformer-big. The upstream conversion of this separate-vocabulary (sepvoc) model ships only the target vocabulary as vocab.json (it covers 21% of source.spm's pieces), so the upstream MarianTokenizer feeds wrong ids and the model outputs nonsense, also in PyTorch. The encoder expects source.spm's own ids: vocab.json is rebuilt from source.spm and the upstream vocab.json ships as target_vocab.json. The model card's template text says a target token is required but lists none; no >>xxx<< tokens exist, so none is used.
